questions.q: What is the Production environment used for?
options: Where the company's real, live business runs — real invoices, payments, and financial statements
Testing new configuration before it's validated
Training new employees exclusively
Only running quarterly update previews
questions.explain: Production is the real, live environment — mistakes here have real financial and operational consequences, which is why new changes are tested elsewhere first.

options: Restarting the servers each night
Copying Production's data into a non-production environment, overwriting what was there
Deleting all data in Production
A quarterly update applied only to non-production
questions.explain: An environment refresh copies Production data into non-production to keep test data realistic, but it overwrites whatever was previously in that non-production environment.

questions.q: Why can an environment refresh be disruptive to an implementation team?
options: It has no real effect on anyone's work
It permanently deletes the Production environment
It can wipe out configuration work in progress in the non-production environment if it hasn't been migrated elsewhere first
It prevents Production from ever being updated again
questions.explain: Because a refresh overwrites non-production with Production's data, any unmigrated configuration work there can be lost, so teams plan around refresh schedules.

questions.q: How does configuration typically move between Oracle Fusion Cloud environments, compared to an on-premises product?
options: Through a traditional compiled code deployment, just like on-premises software
It cannot move between environments at all
Only Oracle support engineers can move configuration, never the customer
Through exporting setup from one environment and importing it into another, via Setup and Maintenance
questions.explain: Instead of deploying compiled code, Fusion Cloud configuration is exported from one environment and imported into another through the Setup and Maintenance work area.

questions.q: What is the general purpose of a non-production (Test) environment?
options: A safe space to build and test changes before they reach the real, live Production environment
To permanently replace Production once testing is complete
To store old data no longer needed anywhere
To run only quarterly marketing reports
questions.explain: Non-production environments exist so configuration and testing happen safely, away from real business transactions, before changes move to Production.
